memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And after the seven days the floodwaters came on the earth... On that very day Noah and his sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, together with his wife and the wives of his three sons, entered the ark... Then the Lord shut him in. - Gen 7:10-13, 16 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is one of the most moving details in the whole flood account: "Then the Lord shut him in." Noah did not close the door of the ark himself. God did. The same hand that invited Noah in now sealed him safely inside. Noah did not have to hold the door against the rising waters or worry whether it would keep. God shut it, and God kept it shut.

Think of the security in that. Once God closed the door, no flood could break it open, and nothing could wash Noah out. His safety did not depend on his own grip or strength; it rested entirely on the God who had shut him in. Noah was safe not because he held on to God, but because God held on to him.

This is the believer's security too. Jesus said of His sheep, "no one will snatch them out of my hand" (John 10:28). Those who are in Christ are shut in by God Himself, kept safe by His power, not their own. We are "shielded by God's power" (1 Pet 1:5).

If you are trusting Christ, you can rest. You did not save yourself, and you do not keep yourself. The God who brought you in has shut the door behind you, and His hand will hold you through every storm. What perfect peace, to be shut in by God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you rest in the truth that God keeps you, not your own strength?
- How does "the Lord shut him in" bring you peace today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that my safety rests in Your hand, not my own grip. Thank You that in Christ You have shut me in, and no storm can wash me out. Give me peace in Your keeping.
